greet.line: Another one walks in from the road. You have the look of someone who woke somewhere they did not lie down.

place.line: The Gloaming. The country under the country. Up there they call it a dream, when they call it anything at all.

why.line: The moon has not moved in nine nights. Something under the Keep is turning in its sleep. Go to the dark water and find the Pale Wanderer. He listens to the lake.

keep.line: If I knew that, I would not need you.

greet.line: Speak to Velloran. We are only here to listen.
Don't mind me. Tall folk talk, I smoke. Between us we get very little done.

talk.line: The moon, the Keep, the end of everything. Same as last time. Same as the time before.

greet.line: The water is very still tonight. That is how you know it is listening back.

sent.line: Then walk the cobbled road to the end, to Vaelmoor Keep. Whatever wakes below it is dreaming of the surface. Do not let it finish the dream.

greet.line: I came here to wash the blood from my armour. That was a long time ago. The water never gets any cleaner.

options.text: Sir Aldric of Hollowford says it is done. You can stop.

aldric.line: ...Hollowford. A green door. The water... look at it. It is clear. I can see the stones on the bottom. Tell him I am coming home. Tell him to leave the door open.

told.line: The water is clear now. I am only waiting for the moon to move, and then I walk home.

greet.line: Mm. Not yet. Wake me when the moon moves.

offer.line: It takes the skull without a sound. For a moment the green light in its ribs burns like a lantern.

greet.line: The moon has been full for nine nights. It should not be. Something under the hills is holding it there.

under.line: Old barrows. Doors that go down further than they should. North, up the lane through Hollowford and out of its north gate. The town built its inn with its back to it. Go down, and you will dream with your eyes open.

greet.line: Hush. It only lands for those who stand very still. I have been standing still for a hundred years.
Heh. Want across? Everyone wants across. Nobody ever says to where.
Kneel or pass. The court has been in session since before your sun was lit.
Careful where you step, there's a dead man down the road and I'd rather not join him. Ysolde. I sell, I buy, I don't ask where it came from. You look like you woke up in a ditch.

again.line: Back again. Buying, selling, or just admiring the cart?

options.text: That strongbox of yours. What's in it?

body.line: West of here, off the road. Wolves didn't kill him, I'll tell you that much. Took his purse and left his sword, which tells you they weren't thieves. Search him if you've the stomach. I didn't.

road.line: Hollowford, if the moon ever moves. Nine nights it's hung there like a lamp nobody can blow out. People in town have started forgetting things. Names. Their own front doors.

box.line: My business. Locked, and staying that way.

options.text: You could at least give a stranger a discount.

box_yes.line: Hah. You've an honest face under all that dirt. Here, a few picks for the road. Don't use them on my strongbox.

town.line: North, up the lane past the cottage. Inn, chapel, a smith who overcharges, and a hundred people who keep forgetting what they came out of the house for. Maren at the inn will put you up, if you have coin.

greet.line: Welcome to the Barrow's Back. Mind the step, it's older than the door. You're not from Hollowford. I'd know. I still know everyone. For now.

again.line: Back again. Bread's yesterday's, mead's last year's. The moon's been the same for nine nights, so who's counting.

options.text: The bell rang. Is it better?
Who is the old man at the table?

forget.line: Since the moon stuck, people lose things. Not keys. Names. Old Jory walked into the river because he forgot it was there. Sir Aldric stands at the well all night because he can't remember which house is his. Brother Cass says it's the bell. Rang every night for three hundred years, and now it doesn't.

options.text: Where do I find Brother Cass?

cass.line: The chapel, west side of the square. You'll hear him before you see him, he reads the names out loud. Says if somebody hears a name, it's still kept.

after.line: Aldric came in and paid his tab. Thirty years, he's never once paid his tab. Whatever you did, I'll pour you one on the house. Just the one.

bram.line: Bram. Drinks here, sleeps here when I let him. He used to be the gravedigger, back when we buried people up at the barrow. Don't buy him a drink. Everybody buys him a drink.

bed.line: Top of the stairs, the room with the moon in the window. They all have the moon in the window. Sleep well.

nobed.line: Ten gold. I've a soft heart and a hard ledger, and the ledger wins.

greet.line: ...Hesper the weaver. Tam Rook. Old Jory, who walked into the river. ...Forgive me. If I say them aloud, someone has heard them. Then they are kept. Are you here to give me a name?

options.text: Why has the town started forgetting?
Can you teach me to heal?

why.line: The barrow behind the inn was the valley's first grave. Our bell was hung to call the sleeping back to their beds every night, so that nothing below would keep them. The night the moon stopped, something came up the barrow road and took the clapper. Since then the bell has no voice, and the sleeping do not come back. Not all the way.

what.line: The Hollow Ones. They were the barrow-wardens once, when wardens were buried with their duty. They stand at the door now and keep anything from leaving. The clapper will be with them, at the barrow door, north up the lane.

go.line: North up the lane, through the gate, past Hale. Do not let them touch you, they take more than blood. Go with the bell, stranger.

waiting.line: The bell is still quiet. I've written forty names today. Yesterday it was thirty. The clapper is at the barrow door, north up the lane.

options.text: Can you teach me to heal?

clapper.line: Is that... it is. It's cold. It has been under the hill. Give it here, I'll hang it myself. My hands remember how even if the rest of me is going.

fixed.line: It hangs true. But I will not ring it. It should be rung by whoever brought its voice home. The rope is by the tower door.

done.line: Did you hear it go down the valley? I have stopped writing names. I've started crossing them out. Thank you. Here, it isn't much, it's the alms box, but no one has come for alms in nine days.

options.text: Can you teach me to heal?

after.line: Sir Aldric is at the well. Go to him. He'll want to see the face of the one who gave him back his name.

taught.line: Hold the wound in your mind as you hold it in your hand. Healing is only remembering what the body was. There. Better.

poor.line: The chapel takes what you can give, but the lesson costs the candles it burns. Fifty gold.

greet.line: They tell me my name is Aldric. I'll take their word for it. I've been standing at this well trying to think which of these doors is mine. One of them is. I'm nearly sure.

who.line: The knight of Hollowford, Maren says. Thirty years. I have the sword for it, and the knees. The rest of it is... somewhere else.

dream.line: One thing, every night. I'm standing in a lake that glows, under a sky that never lightens, washing blood off my armour, and the water never gets any cleaner. I don't know whose blood. I don't know where the lake is. That part, I remember perfectly.

remember.line: That bell. I heard it and I knew the door. The green one. Thirty years I've walked through it. And her name, my wife's. Elsbeth. I'd lost her name. You gave it back. A man shouldn't need a stranger to give him back his own wife's name.

options.text: The lake you dreamed of. Is it real?

lake.line: It's real. It's under the hills, past the barrow, where the country dreams. Part of me is still down there, washing. If you go down, tell him... tell me... it's done, and I can stop. And take this. I don't need a sword to stand by a well.

thanks.line: The green door. Elsbeth. I keep saying them so I keep them. Go well, friend.

greet.line: Eh? Not you. You're not who I was waiting for. Who was I waiting for? Doesn't matter. You buying?

options.text: You look like you have a story.
What was it like, digging graves at the barrow?

barrow.line: Cold. We stopped putting folk up there when the Hollow Ones started standing about. Before that, you'd dig, and you'd hear them under you. Like someone shifting in bed in the next room.

nostory.line: A story? I've got a thirst. The story comes after the thirst.

secret.line: Ahh. That's the stuff. Listen. I hid a box once. Behind the chapel, under the woodpile, years back, when I had things worth hiding. I keep forgetting it's there. Next week I'll forget it entirely. Take it. Somebody should have it who'll remember.

found.line: Well? Was it there? Don't tell me what was in it. I'd only want it back.

where.line: Behind the chapel. Woodpile. I said woodpile, didn't I? It's locked. I had a key once. Had a lot of things once.

thanks.line: Good. Good. Then it's kept. Here's to you, and to the box, and to whatever I was waiting for.

done.line: Box? What box? ...I'm joking. I'm mostly joking.

greet.line: I'm drawing the moon so I remember what it looked like when it moved. Mam says it'll move again. I can't remember Mam's name. Isn't that silly? I'm drawing her too, so I don't lose her face.

options.text: Why do you think everyone is forgetting?

why.line: Brother Cass says the bell has to ring or the sleepy people don't come back from the hill. I don't sleep. I'm not going up the hill.

after.line: Tilde! Her name is Tilde! I remembered when the bell went. I'm going to write it on everything.

greet.line: North gate. Past here it's the barrow road, and the Hollow Ones on it. I'm to stop anyone going up. I'm also to stop anyone coming down. So far it's only been the second sort I worry about.

options.text: I'm going up to the barrow.
Tell me about the Hollow Ones.

up.line: Then I didn't see you. If you come back, come back yourself. If something comes back wearing you, I'll know. I've got a list of questions.

hollow.line: Slow. Heavy. They lean in before they swing, you'll see it coming. Get behind something, or get your shield up at the right moment, and they rock back on their heels. That's when you hit them.

tip.line: Between us, the one with the clapper stands nearest the door. They never sleep, but they don't look up much. Come round the side, crouched, and you might get a blade in before it knows you're there.

notip.line: That's all I'm paid to say. I'm not paid much.

after.line: Heard the bell from up here. Remembered my brother's birthday. I'd missed it six days. He'll forgive me. He forgot too.

options.text: Tell me about the Hollow Ones.

greet.line: Forge is the one thing I don't forget. Iron's got a memory of its own, you see. Bend it once and it remembers. Need something?

options.text: Teach me to use a blade.

smith.line: Watch the colour, not the clock. Cherry red, then strike. There. You'll ruin a few ingots before it sticks.

blade.line: Don't swing from the arm, swing from the hip. Let the steel do the work, it wants to. There. Again. Better.

poor.line: Forty gold. Coal isn't free and neither am I.
